card.title: General and Electronic Concepts of Oxidation and Reduction

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Redox is electron bookkeeping: **oxidation is loss, reduction is gain** (OIL RIG), and because electrons are conserved the two always run together — one species climbs in oxidation number while another falls. The **oxidising agent** accepts electrons and is itself reduced (KMnO₄, K₂Cr₂O₇, O₂, F₂); the **reducing agent** donates them and is itself oxidised (Zn, H₂, CO, C) — role and fate are always opposite.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Agent vs fate:** the oxidising agent is reduced; the reducing agent is oxidised — name the *role* from what happens to the *other* species.  ·  **Displacement direction:** the metal higher in the series displaces the lower metal's ion — students often reverse it; Zn (higher) displaces Cu, never the reverse.

rows.text: ***The copper coin trick*** — an iron nail dropped in CuSO₄ comes out copper-plated: Fe (higher in the series) displaces Cu²⁺; the same logic that corrodes pipes and runs the classic displacement practical.

rows.text: OIL RIG. Agent-fate flip: "oxidant is reduced". Series mnemonic: "Li K Ba Ca Na Mg Al Zn Fe Pb H Cu Hg Ag Au". Halogen oxidising power: "F Cl Br I falls". H₂O₂ pivot: −1 between 0 and −2.

Identify each in Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.** — An **oxidising agent** is a species that accepts electrons and is itself reduced in the process; a **reducing agent** is a species that donates electrons and is itself oxidised.…  ·  **NEB 2024 (3m): What is the electrochemical series? Explain why zinc displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.** — The **electrochemical series** is the arrangement of elements in order of their standard electrode potentials, i.e. their tendency to be reduced (equivalently, the inverse of their tendency to be oxidised).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For agent-identification answers, write the half-reactions first — the species oxidised is the reducing agent, the species reduced is the oxidising agent. For H₂O₂, give one balanced equation per role; unbalanced pairs lose the chemistry mark.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The intermediate-oxidation-state rule powers H₂O₂'s dual behaviour and all disproportionation: an element between two accessible states can move both ways; an element at an extreme (F at −1 floor) cannot.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: OIL RIG: oxidation = loss of electrons/ON increase; reduction = gain/ON decrease; both simultaneous. Oxidising agent accepts e⁻ (is reduced): KMnO₄, K₂Cr₂O₇, F₂, O₂. Reducing agent donates e⁻ (is oxidised): Zn, H₂, CO, C.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Respiration is a redox relay: glucose is oxidised (C from 0 toward +4) while O₂ is reduced (0 → −2 in water) — the same electron accounting as a zinc-copper cell, at 37 °C.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Electron Accounting for Every Reaction Burning, rusting, respiration, plating and batteries all share one bookkeeping system: **oxidation–reduction (redox)**. The modern definition is electronic — oxidation is electron **loss**, reduction is electron **gain** — and every redox reaction is a transfer: one species loses what another gains,…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The electronic concept - **Oxidation:** loss of electrons — Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻; Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻. - **Reduction:** gain of electrons — Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu; Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻. - The two always occur **together** — electrons lost must be gained somewhere; a half-reaction alone cannot happen.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Oxidation** | Loss of electrons / increase in oxidation number | Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ | | **Reduction** | Gain of electrons / decrease in oxidation number | Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu | | **Oxidising agent** | Accepts electrons; is reduced | KMnO₄, F₂ | | **Reducing agent** | Donates electrons; is oxidised…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Comparison Tables **Oxidation vs reduction — the full mirror** | Basis | Oxidation | Reduction | |---|---|---| | Electrons | Lost | Gained | | Oxidation number | Increases | Decreases | | Oxygen/hydrogen (classical) | Gains O / loses H | Gains H / loses O | | Agent role | The species is the **reducing agent** |…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **The agent does the opposite of its name:** an oxidising agent does not get oxidised — it *causes* oxidation and is itself reduced. Role and fate are opposite; exams punish swapping them.  ·  **Oxidation number is not charge:** Mn is +7 in KMnO₄ but no Mn⁷⁺ ion floats in the solution — oxidation numbers are bookkeeping, not ionic charges.
